practice: Continuous deployment in small batches, every change shipped as soon as it passes
claims_to_improve: throughput without a quality loss
loop_element: landing: one project per pull request, merged in the same run
not_carried_over: Release engineers, on-call and customer exposure; an agent run has no users to page

practice: Lightweight review whose value is knowledge transfer and awareness as well as defects
claims_to_improve: fewer defects, shared understanding
loop_element: review of a pull request before merge
not_carried_over: Knowledge transfer and team awareness only help people who stay and learn; a session forgets

practice: Every change reviewed, changes kept small, reviews fast
claims_to_improve: code quality, speed of review (evidence: log of 9 million changes plus survey)
loop_element: review and the blind audit pass of swe-audit
status: partly adopted (audit pass exists, not per change)
not_carried_over: Reviewer latency and social cost; an agent reviewer is cheap but shares the author model family

practice: One repository for all code, atomic cross-project change and trunk-based development
claims_to_improve: shared versioning, easy large refactors
loop_element: this repository and the oss-monorepo mirror
not_carried_over: Custom tooling budget; here the cost is mirror drift and README and projects.json merge conflicts

practice: Static analysis in the review flow, with a path to report and remove noisy checks
claims_to_improve: catch defects early, keep developer trust
loop_element: CI checks: citation, README and number checks on every pull request
not_carried_over: Developer trust and click-through rates; for agents the equivalent is the check false-positive rate

practice: Fault injection in production to find weaknesses before they cause outages
claims_to_improve: resilience of distributed systems
loop_element: harness resilience: blocked network, missing packages, hung tools
not_carried_over: Production traffic and customers; the loop has no production to break

practice: Fixed time, variable scope: a set appetite and a circuit breaker that gives no automatic extension
claims_to_improve: work finishes, fewer open-ended projects
loop_element: run scoping: finish one project small enough to merge, else drop it
not_carried_over: Six-week cycles and a betting table sized for people; a run is hours, not weeks

practice: Do things that do not scale: hand-recruit and hand-serve the first users
claims_to_improve: early traction and learning
loop_element: owner spot-checks of runs
not_carried_over: Founder time is the scarce input; agent labour is not, and the loop has no users to recruit

practice: Error budget: a reliability target that gates release speed
claims_to_improve: settles the speed-versus-reliability argument with a number
loop_element: integrity budget: a prompt version that exceeds an audited defect rate cannot be promoted
status: partly adopted (prompt.md: integrity is a hard constraint)
not_carried_over: Pager load and SLOs on services; the analogue is the audited defect rate from swe-audit

practice: Productivity is multidimensional: use several measures, at least one perceptual
claims_to_improve: guard against optimising one number
loop_element: the track metric: correct, useful and valuable, with throughput
not_carried_over: Satisfaction and well-being; no agent equivalent beyond the owner

practice: Small autonomous cross-functional teams that own a product area
evidence: description of a structure, no outcome data
claims_to_improve: less coordination, faster decisions
loop_element: parallel scheduled runs picking tracks
not_carried_over: Headcount, co-location and culture; runs start in the same minute with no memory of each other

practice: Measure delivery throughput together with stability (lead time, deploy frequency, change failure rate, time to restore)
claims_to_improve: teams improve both speed and reliability (evidence: survey of firms)
loop_element: the ledger: runs, merged projects, reverts and fix-ups together
not_carried_over: Survey of human teams; a ledger row is a run, not a team

practice: Run the smallest experiment that completes one build-measure-learn turn, then decide to pivot or persevere
claims_to_improve: less wasted effort on products nobody wants
loop_element: choosing the next milestone by what the previous project's result says, and stopping a track that returns nothing
not_carried_over: Customers and revenue; a run has no market to learn from, only a ledger and a reviewer, and the book offers no outcome data in what was checked

practice: Treat maintenance and rework as a measured share of engineering time
claims_to_improve: exposes time lost to debugging and refactoring
loop_element: the ledger's rework and duplicate-work signals
not_carried_over: Hours per week of human developers; here the unit is tokens and runs, which the ledger does not yet record

practice: Test the restore, not just the backup, and give every safety mechanism a named owner whose alerts reach someone
claims_to_improve: no silent loss of data when a safety net is needed
loop_element: guards and test suites that skip silently, so a green means nothing ran
status: partly adopted (oss-monorepo guard_state.py lists suites that skip; nothing here does)
not_carried_over: An on-call person reads alert email; an agent session reads only what the next brief tells it to

practice: Remove dead code and never reuse a flag; deploy by a written, checked procedure to every target, not most of them
claims_to_improve: no partial deploy that wakes old behaviour
loop_element: landing to both copies: this repository and the oss-monorepo research/ mirror (retired at cutover)
status: adopted (the two copies were merged into one repository at the 2026-10-16 cutover, so no second copy can miss a deploy; unlanded_work.py still checks branches)
not_carried_over: Financial exposure per minute and a single deploy window; a stale mirror costs readers, not money

practice: Protect makers' time: work in blocks of at least half a day, with meetings bunched at the edges
claims_to_improve: deep work, fewer fragmented afternoons
loop_element: an owner redirecting a session mid-run
not_carried_over: A session has no calendar and does not lose context to a meeting; the analogue, a mid-run change of brief, is rare and cheap here

practice: Small plain-language issues with one owner, fixed 1 to 2 week cycles with automatic rollover, quality work mixed into every cycle
claims_to_improve: focus, steady quality, no estimation ceremony
loop_element: milestone claims in PROJECTS.md and one milestone per run
status: partly adopted (runs claim one milestone; no cycle or rollover of unfinished work)
not_carried_over: Rollover relies on a person remembering the issue; a session needs it written down, and a share of quality work needs a scheduler, not a habit

practice: Give every change a measured resource budget before it ships everywhere: profile each change inside the test suite, keep the protection that caps runaway cost, and stage the rollout
claims_to_improve: no change that passes its tests but exhausts a shared resource in production
loop_element: test suites and checks that run past the harness limit (CLAUDE.md names the 10-minute tool cap and the long node suites)
status: not adopted (suites have no runtime budget, and a run that times out learns it only at the end)
not_carried_over: Global CPU on a live network versus a session's tool timeout; the transferable part is a runtime budget per suite, not a staged global rollout

practice: Run blameless postmortems: collect accounts from several perspectives, ask how the accident became possible, and do not punish the person involved
claims_to_improve: learning from failure without hiding it
loop_element: each run record's errors, doc_friction and deviations fields, and the review track that reads them
status: adopted (prompts/runs records ask each run for errors and doc friction; the review track reads them)
not_carried_over: Blame, fear and careers do not apply to a session; the gap is that a record is one account, written by the run itself, with no second perspective

practice: Write the press release and FAQ for the finished work before building it, so the customer value is argued first
claims_to_improve: build the right thing, cut work nobody wants
loop_element: the README question and the PROJECTS.md milestone text that a run reads before it claims work
status: partly adopted (a project README opens with the question it answers; no customer-facing release is drafted before the build)
not_carried_over: The document is a debate between people over days; a session reads a milestone line and starts, so the check would have to be a short gate against the finished-state bullet list

practice: The team that builds a service runs it: developers own production and hear from customers, with no hand-off to a separate operations team
claims_to_improve: quality and responsiveness from direct ownership
loop_element: the rule that the session that wrote a change opens the pull request and merges it
status: adopted (.github/prompts/land-your-work.md: you own your work until it is merged)
not_carried_over: A pager and customers per session do not exist; ownership here ends at a merged pull request, and nobody reads the result in production

practice: Migrate in reversible stages: write to old and new stores, backfill, switch reads, switch writes, and only then delete the old data
claims_to_improve: changes to a live system with no downtime and a way back at every step
loop_element: layout and tooling changes that other code reads (prompts/runs.jsonl became prompts/runs/, the research mirror cutover)
status: not adopted (batch 4 found a ledger layout change crashed run.py; there was no period when both layouts were written)
not_carried_over: Customer data and live traffic versus files in a git tree; the transferable part is a loader that reads both layouts for a cycle before the old one is deleted

practice: Enforce module boundaries with a checker in CI instead of an agreed social contract
claims_to_improve: boundaries that hold as the codebase and headcount grow
loop_element: the rule that each research project is self-contained under research/<slug>/ and the shared files every run edits (README.md, _homepage/projects.json)
status: partly adopted (_homepage/build.py fails when a project is missing from README.md or projects.json; no check that a project imports nothing from a sibling)
not_carried_over: Boundaries here matter to merge conflicts, not to teams owning code; the shared index files stay a collision point however clean the directories are

practice: No backlog: an idea that matters is pitched again, so nobody grooms a queue
claims_to_improve: no time spent on stale lists, work chosen fresh each cycle
loop_element: the queues in portfolio/ and the 'next steps' lists that runs read
status: partly adopted (CLAUDE.md says not to maintain admin queues; PROJECTS.md milestones are still a standing list)
not_carried_over: Basecamp pitches are argued by people with memory of last cycle; a session has none, so a written list is what carries an idea between runs
